sections.text: The Guardian has published a physics puzzle originally posed by Isaac Newton in 1679. The puzzle asks where an object dropped from a high tower will land, taking the Earth's rotation into account.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The correspondence between Newton and Robert Hooke about this problem rekindled Newton's interest in gravity and motion. This ultimately led to his formulation of classical physics in the Principia. The puzzle was suggested by David Acheson, an emeritus professor of maths at Oxford.
